context: Sho-young describes a left-handed friend to Hiroshi-elder.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: おじいちゃん、友達、左利きなんよ!
lines.style: Bright, eager delivery. Quick opening beat—he's excited to share this discovery. Warm and engaged, but still the careful consideration of a six-year-old testing out new knowledge with an elder.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.style: Gentle, measured response. Soft Kansai lilt. Leans into the observation with genuine interest—not placating, but truly considering what the boy has noticed. Warm fondness underneath.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 茶色の鉛筆、上手に使うの!
lines.en: He uses his brown pencil really well!
lines.style: Animated, observational. High-spirited but not performing—just a child noticing and wanting to report the detail. Warm and bright, building on his excitement from before.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 機嫌、良さそうな子やな。
lines.style: Soft, approving observation. Kansai warmth. He's reading between the lines—not just accepting what Sho says, but hearing what matters underneath. Gentle, appreciative, with the ease of someone who knows how to listen to children.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.jp: 優しい子で、深く、仲良し!
lines.en: He's kind, and we're real close friends.
lines.style: Soft, content delivery. The words come a little slower here—Sho is expressing something that matters. Not boastful, just stating a quiet fact about someone he cares for. Genuine warmth.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.en: That's the kind of friend to treasure.
lines.style: Tender but steady. Kansai ease. A light instruction—not lecturing, but offering something wise in the gentlest way. The grandfather's few words carry weight, delivered with quiet affection and the confidence of someone who knows what matters.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: Yeah, every day with him is fun.
lines.style: Bright, simple affirmation. Soft cheerfulness—he's agreeing with something he already knows, and saying it out loud makes him happy. Warm, innocent, genuine.
